question: What has Raymond James said about its affiliation models, and has the mix shifted?

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says the firm offers multiple affiliation options, which it calls AdvisorChoice®. Advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division. It describes employee advisors as working in a traditional branch with local management and administrative staff, serving predominantly retail clients, and paid primarily through a payout on revenues they generate.

Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists five AdvisorChoice® options: Traditional Employee ("book ownership"), Advisor Select ("Lead your own branch with access to administrative support and full corporate benefits"), Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA ("true autonomy" for fee-only practices). A separate RIA & Custody Services option is also listed.

The same page (as of 2026-04-21) gives headline terms. Traditional Employee: minimum 5 years of experience, up to 50% payout and a full employee benefits offering. Advisor Select: 70-80% gross payout, with a minimum of $3.5 million in annual branch fees and commission revenue. Independent Contractor: 81% to 90% payout, with a third-party benefits package. Corporate RIA: 81% to 90% payout, with minimum $50 million in assets under advisement. Bank & Credit Union: compensation is set by the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James. RIA & Custody Services: compensation is determined by the RIA or broker/dealer, who is also responsible for compliance.

Raymond James's own recruiting pages (content as of dates in 2026) pitch each model separately. Advisor Select (as of 2026-03-11) is "an employee affiliation option" for entrepreneurial advisors who run their branch's P&L "to earn a higher rate on production". The Independent Advisor page (as of 2026-05-19) offers "a partnership in independence" backed by a self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer. The Corporate RIA is described as an "all-inclusive" model that streamlines the burdens of an RIA. The RCS page (as of 2026-07-12) promises "complete freedom and control", "free from retail conflict", with the user choosing "as much – or as little" of the firm's support as needed.

On earnings calls, management frames the value proposition as one "best of both worlds" offer across all options. On the 2Q FY25 call (April 2025) and the 3Q FY25 call (October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry described a combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions that "continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options". On the 4Q FY25 call (January 2026) he said the firm has "the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody", with "critical mass and decades of experience in all of them". On the call published 2026-07-22 he said the firm is "agnostic" on how an advisor affiliates and "indifferent" to it.

On the call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry said advisors differ in how they spend their time across the options. Some want to spend close to 100% of their time on books of business and clients, which he said is "more aligned with the employee affiliation option". Others also want to run a business: building a team, paying for benefits, real estate and legal matters.

The 2025 10-K (as of September 30) shows financial advisors by channel. Employees: 3,878 (2025), 3,826 (2024), 3,693 (2023). Independent contractors: 5,065 (2025), 4,961 (2024), 5,019 (2023). Total: 8,943, 8,787 and 8,712. RCS advisors are not included in this advisor metric, although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.

On the 3Q FY24 call (October 2024), then-CEO Paul Reilly said RCS had "by far the highest percentage growth". In total dollars the lead alternates: "a couple of years ago, it was independent. This year, the employee channel really led the way." He said the old pattern that independents grow faster in up markets is no longer seen: "It is really just where we can meet the teams that like an affiliation option." RCS client assets were $181 billion, up 36% over the prior year.

On the 4Q FY24 call (January 2025), RCS finished the quarter with $188 billion of client assets under administration, up 28% year-over-year. The investor-day deck (published 2025-06-05), in a slide titled "Strong asset growth across our multiple affiliation models", charts domestic PCG AUA for Employee, Independent contractor and RCS between Mar. 31, 2020 and Mar. 31, 2025. It labels 5-year CAGRs of 32%, 11%, 14% and 14%. The extracted text does not tie each figure to a channel.

On the 2Q FY25 call (July 2025), Shoukry said the firm sees "good success across all of our affiliation options". He said "the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher", with very good success in the employee and independent RIA options as well.

The 10-Q filings show PCG AUA from firms affiliated through RCS. On Dec 31, 2025 it was $224.6 billion, versus $217.3 billion on Sep 30, 2025 and $188.2 billion on Dec 31, 2024. On Jun 30, 2026 it was $251.3 billion, versus $228.2 billion on Mar 31, 2026 and $201.6 billion on Jun 30, 2025. The firm says RCS growth is "partially due to transfers into RCS from our other financial advisor channels", but it does not expect such transfers to significantly impact results of operations.

On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said "we're actually seeing pretty good uptick in the employee affiliation option as well". He said the "mix shift" he had referred to concerned the compensation ratio, because of "the payout difference in the independent channel versus the employee channel". He added that independent-side catalysts should not "overshadow" employee-side success, which "continues to tick up".

The firm has recruited across channels, with each period's figures stated on its call. Recruited advisors' trailing 12-month production at previous firms (domestic independent contractor and employee channels) and client assets:
- FY24 (call published 2024-10-23): approximately $335 million and $56.7 billion.
- FY25 (call published 2025-10-22): $407 million, up 21%, and approximately $58 billion; nearly $63 billion in total client assets across all platforms including RAA and Custody Services.
- Past 12 months to the call published 2026-01-28: nearly $460 million and over $63 billion; more than $69 billion across all platforms.
- Quarter reported 2026-04-22: $141 million and nearly $21 billion.
- Quarter reported 2026-07-22: $156 million and nearly $23 billion; $393 million and more than $56 billion for the first 9 months of the fiscal year.

Management describes recruiting as broad-based across models. On the call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry said recruiting has been "broad-based across all of our affiliation options, the employee, independent contractor, and the RAA custody channels". On the call published 2026-07-22 he said the source of recruiting success and the pipeline "remains diverse across our affiliation options". On the call published 2025-07-23 he said M&A-driven catalysts, "particularly on the independent side", contributed to the acceleration in the pipeline but success was not concentrated there. On the call published 2026-04-22 he cited an "uptick of commits" in the employee option.

On moves out of a model, Reilly said on the 3Q FY24 call (October 2024) that a couple of OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division were leaving. Roughly $3 billion of AUA left in the fiscal fourth quarter, with approximately $5 billion more expected early in fiscal 2025. On the call published 2025-01-29 he cited the departure of primarily one large branch in the independent contractor division, with an impact of approximately $5 billion of AUA.

The 2025 10-K names the risk of advisors departing traditional firms, including "to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs", some PE-backed. It says that if departures continue or accelerate, including transition "to an unaffiliated RIA channel", this could adversely affect PCG results. The firm says it seeks to mitigate this through succession planning and a broad range of services.

Management's stated priorities on recruiting and retention, with the date of each call:
- Call published 2026-04-22: Shoukry said the firm prefers to "recruit 1 by 1" rather than acquire, because "100% of the transition assistance is going to retention of the adviser". He said it has ramped up recruiting substantially year over year and broken out recruiting and retention costs.
- Call published 2026-07-22: he said recruiting "is not something you could turn on and off quarter-to-quarter" and that consistency across affiliation options is critical.
- Call published 2026-04-22: he said continued investment in automation, process improvement and AI is part of "more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend".

On competition, Shoukry said on the call published 2025-07-23 that PE-backed roll-ups have been "extremely aggressive" in paying higher multiples. He said "we are still seeing pressure on the existing advisor base, private equity", and that roll-ups "compete with big checks" in the absence of a value proposition. On the call published 2026-01-28 he said competition has increased, but the firm feels it has "in some ways, less competition than ever". He cited its long-term focus, its commitment to remaining independent and its technology investment of about $1 billion, which he said many similar-culture competitors do not match. On the call published 2026-04-22 he said private equity "has certainly been competitive over the last 5 years".

The 2025 10-K names competitive risks. It describes "a highly competitive recruiting environment" tied to the industry-wide departure of advisors to independent RIAs. It also notes claims of unfair hiring practices, and that participation in the voluntary Protocol for Broker Recruiting could change if competitors withdraw.

Where management acknowledges ground lost: the independent contractor division lost OSJ relationships and a large branch in fiscal 2024-25, with roughly $3 billion, $5 billion and approximately $5 billion of AUA cited across the calls. Management also pointed to a compensation-ratio effect from a shift toward the independent channel, because of the payout difference versus the employee channel.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) reports that Shoukry said recruiting success is spread across all channels. The independent contractor channel sees the most interest in dollar volume, and the RIA custody division, on a smaller base, is growing at a high percentage rate. The article also says Raymond James no longer reports advisor headcount and had about 8,900 advisors the last time it was broken out. It cites $538 million of recruited trailing 12-month production for FY2026, versus $407 million prior year, and more than $82 billion in client assets.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Trade press in 2026 describes moves by model. Teams joined the employee channel (RJA) from UBS (2026-08-21), from Truist (2026-11-05) and from PNC Private Bank (2026-11-06). Independent channel additions came from Ameriprise (2026-08-26) and Commonwealth (2026-09-24). A Southwest Florida team joined the Financial Institutions Division (2026-11-05). Outflows reported: a $1.1 billion Georgia team left Raymond James Financial Services for an independent RIA with Fidelity custody (2026-10-27). Four practices (about $1 billion) left RJFS for the Ascentis RIA platform while continuing to use Raymond James as primary custodian (2026-10-08). Two California teams that managed roughly $545 million at Raymond James joined FiNet (2026-08-28).
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

gaps.what: Advisor and asset mix by affiliation model after September 30, 2025 is not found: the evidence has employee/independent contractor advisor counts only to FY2025, and a trade report says headcount is no longer broken out. Separate asset totals for the employee and independent contractor channels are not disclosed in the filings provided, apart from the RCS total and an investor-day chart whose figures are not labeled by channel.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James quarterly financial supplements and 10-K/10-Q PCG key-metrics tables; the investor-day deck with legible chart labels.

gaps.what: Attrition or retention figures by affiliation model, and counts of advisors transferring between models (for example into RCS), are not disclosed beyond qualitative statements and RCS growth commentary.
gaps.suggested_source: Management disclosure on advisor transfers between channels (earnings call Q&A, 10-K PCG section) or the firm's investor relations team.

gaps.what: No management statement was found in the evidence saying the firm is pulling back from, or deprioritizing, any specific affiliation model. Management describes all options as being pursued.
gaps.suggested_source: Later earnings-call transcripts and the next 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A discussion of PCG strategy.
